t.E444.agn: In its 2016 re-evaluation EFSA raised the acceptable daily intake (ADI) from 10 to 20 mg/kg body weight and stated that estimated exposure did not exceed this limit in any age group and that there was no safety concern at the authorised uses. JECFA had also set an ADI of 0-20 mg/kg body weight in 1996.
t.E444.body: In humans, it has been reported that most (88% or more) of orally ingested sucrose acetate isobutyrate is absorbed.
t.E444.found.1: Cloudy flavoured alcoholic drinks with less than 15% alcohol
t.E444.prod: It is produced by modifying a plant raw material through a chemical reaction.
t.E444.regx.0: Re-evaluated; ADI of 20 mg/kg body weight per day (instead of the previous 10 mg/kg), exposure does not exceed the ADI.
t.E444.regx.1: ADI of 0-20 mg/kg body weight per day.
t.E444.summary: A weighting agent produced from sugar. It prevents flavouring oils from rising to the surface in cloudy fruit drinks.
t.E444.what: In cloudy drinks it adjusts the density of flavouring oils so that the cloudy appearance is evenly distributed in the drink (weighting agent).
